beats.say: Inside the cluster, every pod can call every other pod.
beats.text: Every pod can call every pod

beats.say: A namespace is a folder for names. It is not a firewall.
beats.label: A wrong idea
beats.head: A namespace is not a firewall

beats.say: This port has three steps: see the flat network, deny by default, and allow DNS.
beats.label: Port 8 · Network policies

check.prompt: Two policies select the same pod. One allows A, the other allows B. What gets in?
check.why: Policies add up. A pod accepts the union of every rule that selects it.

beats.say: One policy selects every pod and allows nothing. Now all inbound traffic is blocked.
beats.label: Default deny
beats.head: Select all, allow nothing

beats.say: Then you add one small rule for each real path. For example: web to API.
beats.label: Then allow
beats.head: One rule per real path

beats.say: Rules select pods by label. And the rules add up.
beats.label: How rules work
beats.head: Labels again. Rules add up.

check.prompt: After a default-deny egress policy, every call by name times out. Why?
check.why: A lookup goes to the cluster DNS on port 53. Allow that first.

beats.say: You deny all egress. And then every call by name fails.
beats.label: Surprise
beats.head: Every name lookup fails

beats.say: So allow the cluster DNS on port 53 first. Then open what each app needs.
beats.label: The fix
beats.head: Allow DNS on port 53 first

beats.say: Deny by default. Allow each real path. And never forget DNS.
beats.label: Network policies

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
